items.markdown:
Biotin (vitamin B7) supplements `do not promote hair growth` in healthy people who already get enough of the nutrient from their diet.[[1]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5582478/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ph4vXrxtP98)

### Does It Work?

- **Deficiencies are rare:** Most people get plenty of biotin from everyday foods like eggs, meat, fish, nuts, seeds, and sweet potatoes.[[1]](https://blog.walgreens.com/wellness/vitamins-supplements/biotin-for-hair-growth-can-it-help.html)[[2]](https://www.everydayhealth.com/skin-care/does-biotin-help-with-hair-growth-and-loss/)
- **Limited proof:** Clinical evidence shows biotin only helps hair health if you have a documented biotin deficiency or specific medical conditions like alopecia.[[1]](https://health.clevelandclinic.org/is-biotin-as-good-as-advertised-for-your-hair-loss)[[2]](https://www.webmd.com/diet/health-benefits-biotin)
- **Overkill doses:** While the daily recommended intake for adults is about 30 mcg, many over-the-counter supplements contain 5,000 to 10,000 mcg, which your body simply flushes out in your urine.[[1]](https://blog.walgreens.com/wellness/vitamins-supplements/biotin-for-hair-growth-can-it-help.html)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b2hzlez2zDE&t=157)

### Risks and Side Effects

- **Lab test interference:** High doses of biotin can severely skew common blood work—including thyroid tests and cardiac markers (such as troponin for heart attacks)—leading to false results.[[1]](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/OP-25-00693)[[2]](https://www.facebook.com/AADskin/videos/do-biotin-supplements-really-help-with-hair-loss-heres-what-board-certified-derm/1057516907235066/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b2hzlez2zDE&t=157)
- **Washout period:** Doctors recommend stopping biotin supplements 2 to 7 days before having routine blood tests.[[1]](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/OP-25-00693)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b2hzlez2zDE&t=157)

### Better Alternatives for Hair Shedding
If you are experiencing hair loss, common root causes include stress, genetics, or low levels of iron, zinc, or vitamin D rather than a lack of biotin. Proven options include:[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7xhaI2CsG2E&t=27)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ph4vXrxtP98)[[3]](https://www.facebook.com/AADskin/videos/do-biotin-supplements-really-help-with-hair-loss-heres-what-board-certified-derm/1057516907235066/)

- Checking with a board-certified dermatologist or healthcare provider to find the underlying cause.
- Using evidence-based treatments like topical minoxidil.[[1]](https://www.facebook.com/AADskin/videos/do-biotin-supplements-really-help-with-hair-loss-heres-what-board-certified-derm/1057516907235066/)[[2]](https://blog.walgreens.com/wellness/vitamins-supplements/biotin-for-hair-growth-can-it-help.html)[[3]](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/OP-25-00693)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b2hzlez2zDE&t=157)

You can read more detailed guidance on safety and side effects via the [Mayo Clinic Biotin Overview](https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/biotin-oral-route/description/drg-20062359).[[1]](https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/biotin-oral-route/description/drg-20062359)If you'd like, tell me:

- **How long** it has been happening
